    Push-downs of L(T) are modules if two of them are #

    For a Kronecker pair and a quiver morphism p : D → Q, an element z of the path algebra kQ that acts by zero on the push-downs of L(S₋) = Q₀ and of L(P₁), where P₁ = (k, k²) is the projective Kronecker module (L(P₁) is the universal extension of P by Q₀² given by z₁, z₂), acts by zero on the push-down of every L(T) (kills_of_generators). Every vector of L(T) is a sum of images of L(f) for morphisms f : S₋ → T and f : P₁ → T, and the action of kQ on push-downs is natural.

    So the kills condition of covering data with a Kronecker pair reduces to the finite statement that Q₀ and the universal extension are A-modules (PairCoveringData.mk').
